name: Understanding when and why optimization works
gist: Gradient descent and neural network training have surprising behaviors. What are the mathematical principles and limits? Why does noise sometimes help? When do algorithms get stuck?
explain: Gradient descent is the workhorse of machine learning: you compute how wrong your model is (the loss), you compute the direction that reduces wrongness (the gradient), and you step in that direction. It has worked for decades, but it should not work because the theory says it would get stuck. The space of possible model settings has billions of dimensions, with countless local minima (dead ends where many directions go uphill) and saddle points (places where the ground slopes both up and down). If you start at a random place and follow a greedy downhill direction, you should get trapped in an early dead end, yet in practice, gradient descent finds settings that work well. This is a mystery. Why does a simple algorithm succeed in a space that theory says should trap it?

A second puzzle is noise. When you compute gradients on a batch of 32 examples (a tiny fraction of a 1-million-example dataset), the gradient is random—it changes every time you pick a new batch. This noise could slow learning because you are taking random directions, but instead it seems to help, which is surprising. Models trained with noisy batch gradients often generalize better than models trained with accurate full-dataset gradients, which happens because noise pushes the algorithm toward flatter regions of the solution space. Adding noise to the update step, or using momentum, or other tricks seem to point the algorithm toward flatter minima, and flat minima generalize well to new data because they are less sensitive to slight changes. But why does this mechanism work? And when does this break?

Papers study these questions from many angles. Some prove that in certain settings, all critical points (places where the gradient is zero) that are not global minima are unstable saddle points, so gradient descent skips over them. Others show that batch noise acts like a regularizer, biasing the algorithm toward solutions that work well on examples it has not seen. Some researchers analyze what properties of the data and model architecture guarantee success. Others study implicit bias: even without explicit penalties for complexity, gradient descent naturally learns simple patterns first. A few papers show failure cases: settings where the theory does not apply and gradient descent gets stuck. The pattern is that optimization works not by magic, but by mathematical principles that researchers are slowly uncovering.

papers.title: A Tale of Two Smoothness Notions: Adaptive Optimizers and Non-Euclidean Descent
papers.contribution: Proves adaptive smoothness precisely characterizes adaptive optimizer convergence and enables acceleration guarantees unattainable under standard smoothness.

papers.title: Gradient Descent with Large Step Sizes: Chaos and Fractal Convergence Region
papers.contribution: The study shows that near-critical step sizes induce a chaotic regime where adding regularization amplifies sensitivity and generates fractal convergence boundaries.

papers.title: How does the optimizer implicitly bias the model merging loss landscape?
papers.contribution: Proves merging effectiveness depends on effective noise scale combining learning rates, weight decay, batch sizes, and data augmentation, predicting when solutions can be merged.

papers.title: Hyperbolic Aware Minimization: Implicit Bias for Sparsity
papers.contribution: Consistently increases performance even in dense training across vision benchmarks and is especially effective when combined with sparsification methods.

papers.title: Last-Iterate Convergence of Regularized Gradient Methods for Stochastic Monotone Variational Inequalities
papers.contribution: RG attains O(t^{-2/5}) and ROG achieves variance-adaptive O(σ^{4/5} t^{-2/5} + t^{-1}), providing guarantees without knowing horizon.

papers.title: Minor First, Major Last: A Depth-Induced Implicit Bias of Sharpness-Aware Minimization
papers.contribution: For L=2 networks, ℓ∞-SAM converges to unpredictable limit directions dependent on initialization, while ℓ2-SAM exhibits 'sequential feature discovery' where minor coordinates initially dominate then shift to major ones as training progresses.

papers.title: On Densest $k$-Subgraph Mining and Diagonal Loading: Optimization Landscape and Finite-Step Exact Convergence Analysis
papers.contribution: (AAAI 2025) introduced a penalty-based non-convex relaxation that achieves promising empirical performance; however, a rigorous theoretical understanding of its success remains unclear

papers.title: The Implicit Bias of Adam and Muon on Smooth Homogeneous Neural Networks
papers.contribution: Proves Adam maximizes ℓ∞ margin and characterizes hybrid norms for Adam-variants; results extend to smooth homogeneous models with corroborating experiments.

papers.title: Adaptive Sharpness-Aware Minimization with a Polyak-type Step size: A Theory-Grounded Scheduler
papers.contribution: Proves linear convergence for strongly convex and O(1/T) convergence for convex objectives; empirically achieves performance comparable to carefully tuned SAM baselines with substantially reduced tuning.

papers.title: Align-SAM: Seeking Flatter Minima for Better Cross-Subset Alignment
papers.contribution: Align-SAM consistently improves generalization across diverse datasets and challenging settings including noisy labels and limited data scenarios.

papers.title: AutoEP: LLMs-Driven Automation of Hyperparameter Evolution for Metaheuristic Algorithms
papers.contribution: AutoEP consistently outperforms state-of-the-art tuners including neural evolution and other LLM-based methods on three metaheuristics; open-source models like Qwen3-30B match GPT-4 performance.

papers.title: Can Adaptive Gradient Methods Converge under Heavy-Tailed Noise? A Case Study of AdaGrad
papers.contribution: Achieves adaptive-to-tail-index convergence, and develops algorithm-dependent lower bound suggesting minimax optimality is not attainable by AdaGrad.

papers.title: Can Muon Fine-tune Adam-Pretrained Models?
papers.contribution: Demonstrates that LoRA consistently reduces the performance gap between Adam and Muon fine-tuning across language and vision tasks, with mismatch severity correlating with update strength.

papers.title: Conflicting Biases at the Edge of Stability: Norm versus Sharpness Regularization
papers.contribution: Demonstrates that learning rate interpolates between norm and sharpness biases, requiring broader view of implicit regularization capturing dynamic trade-off.

papers.title: Consistent Low-Rank Approximation
papers.contribution: The paper proves recourse bounds ranging from O(k/ε log(nd)) for additive approximation to improved bounds of k^(3/2)/ε² poly log(nd) for multiplicative approximation on integer matrices.

papers.title: Decentralized Online Convex Optimization with Efficient Communication: Improved Algorithm and Lower Bounds
papers.contribution: Achieves improved regret bounds of Õ(ω^{-1/2}ρ^{-1}n√T) and Õ(ω^{-1}ρ^{-2}n ln T) for convex and strongly convex functions, justifying optimality with respect to compression quality and time horizon.

papers.title: Envy-Free Allocation of Indivisible Goods via Noisy Queries
papers.contribution: Optimal query scaling is m^2.5/Delta^2 when negative-envy Delta is not too small, with upper bound via non-adaptive queries and lower bound holding even for adaptive queries.

papers.title: Extra-Merge: Tracing the Rank-1 Subspace of Model Merging in Language Model Pre-Training
papers.contribution: Extra-Merge outperforms standard merging without gradient updates, achieving zero-shot gains on Pythia-12B with consistent improvements across GPT-2 and LLaMA families.

papers.title: Fast Estimation of Wasserstein Distances via Regression on Sliced Wasserstein Distances
papers.contribution: The approach provides better Wasserstein distance approximation than state-of-the-art Wasserstein Wormhole, particularly in low-data regimes, and can accelerate Wormhole training.

papers.title: FedScar: Correcting Geometric Bias for Flatness-Consistent Federated Learning
papers.contribution: Consistently reduces flatness discrepancy and improves generalization under severe heterogeneity over state-of-the-art without additional communication overhead.

papers.title: Fix the Loss, Not the Radius: Rethinking the Adversarial Perturbation of Sharpness-Aware Minimization
papers.contribution: Consistently outperforms SAM and variants across diverse benchmarks and tasks, achieving state-of-the-art generalization.

papers.title: Flatness-Aware Stochastic Gradient Langevin Dynamics
papers.contribution: Non-asymptotic convergence analysis to flatness-biased Gibbs distribution with explicit excess risk guarantees; strong empirical performance on classification and uncertainty tasks.

papers.title: Geometry-Misalignment in Distributional Learning
papers.contribution: Demonstrates sharp separation between Euclidean and geometry-aware optimization, with improvements concentrated in high-misalignment regimes for domain adaptation tasks.

papers.title: Learning the Best Under Constraints: A Duality-Based Framework
papers.contribution: Achieve both theoretical sample complexity bounds and practical computational efficiency via convex duality.

papers.title: Lower Bounds for Frank-Wolfe on Strongly Convex Sets
papers.contribution: Establishes a tight lower bound of Ω(1/√ε), showing known uniform O(1/√ε) guarantees are tight.

papers.title: Momentum Further Constrains Sharpness at the Edge of Stochastic Stability
papers.contribution: Reveals that small batch sizes favor flatter regions via momentum amplification while large batches recover momentum's classical stabilizing effect; aligns with linear stability thresholds.

papers.title: Navigating the Flatlands: Dual Adaptive Sharpness-Aware Minimization for Domain Generalization
papers.contribution: DA-SAM guides model parameters away from anisotropic sharp regions with domain-level guidance, improving domain generalization robustness.

papers.title: Non-Euclidean Gradient Descent Operates at the Edge of Stability
papers.contribution: The framework provides geometry-aware spectral diagnostics for non-Euclidean gradient methods including l-infinity descent and Spectral GD.

papers.title: Revisiting Sharpness-Aware Minimization: A More Faithful and Effective Implementation
papers.contribution: The framework achieves better generalization by more faithfully implementing the SAM objective through explicit maximum direction estimation.

papers.title: Sharpness-Aware Minimization Can Hallucinate Minimizers
papers.contribution: Identifies a failure mode explaining SAM's degradation at large ρ and provides practical mitigation reducing sensitivity to ρ choice.

papers.title: Sharpness-Aware Minimization in Logit Space Efficiently Enhances Direct Preference Optimization
papers.contribution: Logits-SAM consistently improves DPO effectiveness on Pythia-2.8B and Mistral-7B across multiple datasets with negligible computational overhead.

papers.title: Towards Understanding The Calibration Benefits of Sharpness-Aware Minimization
papers.contribution: SAM and CSAM achieve consistently lower calibration errors than other approaches, with theoretical analysis connecting sharpness to calibration properties.
